title: Shaheer Sheikh Plays a Deported NRI Hunting for His Missing Brother. Ab Hoga Hisaab Is Free, Furious, and Uncomfortably Real.
excerpt: Sanjay Kapoor, Mouni Roy, and a Canada immigration racket hiding something horrifying — Amazon MX Player's new revenge drama premieres free on June 18.
body:
The trailer opens with a Punjab that looks nothing like the one Bollywood usually sells you — no mustard fields, no bhangra on rooftops, no old grandmother dispensing life lessons with chai. This Punjab is tense, dusty, and dangerous. **Shaheer Sheikh** stands in the middle of it as Bobby Manocha, a recently deported NRI who has returned to a hometown that doesn't feel like home anymore. His younger brother Bunty, played by **Avinash Mishra** in his streaming debut, has vanished. And nobody seems particularly interested in finding him.

*Ab Hoga Hisaab* drops on **Amazon MX Player on June 18**, and it's free. That alone would make it worth a mention. But what makes this one genuinely important is the story it's telling — and who it's telling it to.

The setup is devastatingly familiar to anyone who's spent time in NRI WhatsApp groups: a family pooling everything to send their youngest abroad. Canada is the promised land. The visa agents are trusted. The money changes hands. And then someone disappears.

> "How far will you go for your own?" — Official tagline

The series, directed by **Divyanshu Malhotra** and produced by **Arré Studio**, pulls back the curtain on a human-trafficking syndicate operating under the cover of an immigration consultancy. It's the kind of story that plays out in news tickers every few months — Punjabi students found dead in shipping containers, families bankrupted by fake agents, entire villages hollowed out by the promise of a foreign passport. *Ab Hoga Hisaab* takes that reality and wraps it in a revenge thriller.

**Sanjay Kapoor** plays Goldy, the powerful local figure at the center of the web. From the trailer, it's clear Kapoor is relishing the villain turn — there's a quiet menace to him that's more effective than any scenery-chewing could be. His performance feels measured, controlled, the kind of villain who never raises his voice because he doesn't need to.

**Mouni Roy** rounds out the principal cast, and while the trailer keeps her cards close, her presence signals the show isn't skimping on star power. **Nimrit Kaur Ahluwalia** and **Harman Singha** fill out an ensemble that balances television familiarity with the kind of dramatic weight this material demands.

But the real surprise here might be Avinash Mishra. The *Bigg Boss 18* standout making his OTT debut as the younger brother whose disappearance drives the narrative — it's canny casting. He's got the screen magnetism and enough existing fan investment to give Bunty's fate real emotional stakes before the first episode even ends.

What makes *Ab Hoga Hisaab* particularly sharp for diaspora audiences is that it doesn't romanticize the NRI dream. Bobby isn't a success story. He's been deported. He's back in Punjab not because he chose to return but because he was sent back. And now he's watching the same machine that chewed him up consume his brother. There's an anger in the trailer that feels personal, earned, and deeply rooted in the specific humiliation of failed immigration — something millions of desi families understand but Bollywood rarely touches.

The show streams free on Amazon MX Player, which means accessibility isn't a barrier. You can watch it on Prime Video, Fire TV, JioTV, and Airtel Xstream as well. For NRI viewers in the US, Canada, and the UK, this is available without a premium subscription wall — a smart move given the subject matter is precisely aimed at communities already paying attention to immigration horror stories in the news.

Six episodes. A revenge arc. A missing brother. A Canada visa scam.

If the writing holds up to the promise of the trailer, *Ab Hoga Hisaab* might be the most relevant Indian series of the summer for anyone who has ever helped a cousin fill out a visa application, wired money to an "agent," or wondered if the dream of abroad was worth the cost.

It premieres June 18. Mark it.
